- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and forecast shows upward momentum, reduce forecast peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment includes recent positive spikes (e.g., > 0.23), model tends to overreact — cap forecast rise after initial spike to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows sharp downward drift after a forecast peak, reduce forecast slope in subsequent days to avoid lagged overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to overcorrect upward — apply downward bias correction to forecast mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 1.5% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% to align with mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model overfits short-term sentiment — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3-day moving average.
